To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a two-stage schema matching approach, the first of which uses mutual information to measure the pair-wise dependency between attributes and construct a dependency graphs and the second stage uses a graph matching algorithm to find matching pairs in the graphs.
(a) the mutual information of the attribute pairs is an important indicator of attribute similarity and that (b) the graph matching algorithm can find matching node pairs with high accuracy.

(1) the use of a dependency graph, constructed using mutual information to capture the pair-wise correlations among the attributes of the tables to be compared, can be a valuable tool in schema matching; (2) a graph matching algorithm can be used to match the nodes of such a dependency graph; and (3) our approach can be a valuable addition to a set (semi) automatic techniques for schema matching, and can be used in conjunction with such techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of schema matching when column names and the data in columns are opaque.
the problem of schema matching in cases where the column names in schemas and the data stored in columns are opaque.
developing a new technique to solve the schema matching problem that can be used in conjunction with other techniques that rely upon the similarity of column names or data values.

the technique proposed in the paper can be used to match schemas that are not amenable to other schema matching techniques, such as those that use string similarity or data value similarity.
the proposed approach is an effective and efficient way to solve the schema matching problem in the presence of "opaque" column names and data.
our approach can be used as a complementary technique in schema matching.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an algorithm that is able to handle schema matching problems that are not solvable with the current techniques.
we have proposed an algorithm that works well even in the absence of any linguistic knowledge and can thus be used to complement the existing approaches.
we have developed a technique that works in the presence of column names and values that are opaque, which is a significant contribution in itself.

even in the presence opaque data values, we can still use the data itself in a meaningful way to match schemas.
the use of mutual information as a dependency measure is an interesting and promising direction for schema matching research.

even in the absence of any meaningful column or data values, it is possible to match schemas by measuring the pair-wise attribute correlation in the tables to find the matching node pairs in dependency graphs.
